title: Maps out of a localised module are the maps out of the module, when the target has invertible actions
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a multiplicative subset S and R-modules M, N on which every element of S acts invertibly, the canonical map from Hom of the localisation into N to Hom of M into N is an isomorphism (statement lines 1387-1396). The proof does not cite the adjunction between localisation and the modules with invertible actions: it shows injectivity by computing that a map on the localisation is determined by its values on M, builds the extension on pairs and checks well-definedness against the equivalence relation, and verifies linearity by a common-denominator computation (proof lines 1398-1428). The explicit well-definedness and linearity checks are the substance, and the author writes them all out. H2.
